messages:
Maya (Support): FYI customer AcmeOps reporting intermittent 502/504 when calling /v1/generate since ~13:10 UTC. They see 'TLS handshake timeout' on their side and 502 from our gateway.
AcmeOps (Customer): Yep, started ~13:08. Some requests succeed but ~30% fail with "TLS handshake timeout" in client logs. We haven't changed anything on our side. cURL shows timeouts too.
Ryan (Oncall): Can you paste the full client error and a timestamp of a failed request? Also which region / host are they hitting?
AcmeOps (Customer): Hitting us-east-1 endpoint: api.redwood-hosted.com. Example failure at 2026-03-15T13:12:07Z. Client log: "upstream handshake timeout after 10s (error: TLS handshake failure)". cURL output:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX'
*   Trying 3.120.45.9:443...
* connect to 3.120.45.9 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-hosted.com port 443: Connection timed out
```

Maya (Support): They also included a traceroute showing packet loss near edge (first hop ok, then jumps). They suspect cert rotation but we rotated certs yesterday at 02:00 UTC and deploy-bot reported success.
deploy-bot: TLS cert rotation for api.redwood-hosted.com completed at 2026-03-14T02:01:12Z. Status: SUCCESS.
Kara (SRE): I'm pulling edge envoy logs for 13:00-13:30 UTC. Seeing a spike in downstream TLS handshake timeouts and a handful of "SSL_read: Connection reset by peer" errors. Also seeing multiple failed OCSP queries to our OCSP responder, timeouts ~1s each.
Ryan (Oncall): Could this be a resolver issue? If client resolvers get stale A records they might hit old IPs without SNI/proxy capacity. Any DNS churn after the cert rotate?
dnsbot: DNS change: A-record rotation for api.redwood-hosted.com propagated to Route53 weight pool at 2026-03-14T02:00:47Z. TTL previous was 300s, new TTL is 60s.
Maya (Support): Customer said their corporate resolver caches beyond TTL (they're using an internal forwarder). They saw an IP with geolocation mismatch (EU ip for us-east endpoint).
AcmeOps (Customer): Confirmed: our resolver returned 54.36.120.11 for ~20 minutes after change, then later returned 3.120.45.9 which worked. When hitting 54.36.120.11 we saw immediate TLS errors.
Kara (SRE): 54.36.120.11 is an old ELB instance that's been decommissioned but not fully drained; it lacks the updated cert chain (missing new intermediate) and no SNI passthrough config. That explains handshake failures and unexpected resets.
Ryan (Oncall): Reasonable path: resolver -> stale IP -> client tries handshake -> server either no matching cert or connection reset -> client times out -> gateway reports 502/504.
Maya (Support): Action items: 1) Notify customer to flush their resolver/cache or use 8.8.8.8 as temporary workaround. 2) SRE to verify decommissioned ELBs are fully removed from DNS/health checks. 3) Add monitoring to detect stale IPs in DNS responses and mismatched cert chains.
Kara (SRE): I'm removing that old instance from the legacy pool and forcing DNS re-propagation. Also adding a health-check rule: if a host presents a cert that doesn't match the canonical SANs, remove from pool. Rolling now.
Kara (SRE): Fix pushed to infra: health-check cert validation gate added and old-instance forcibly removed at 13:42 UTC. I'll watch for errors dropping.
AcmeOps (Customer): Flushed our resolver and switched to 8.8.8.8. After that failures dropped to ~0.1%. Thanks — still seeing a couple of slow requests but nothing like before.
Maya (Support): Can you please run an openssl check against both IPs you previously received? Example command we used:
```
openssl s_client -connect 54.36.120.11:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.com -showcerts -brief
```

AcmeOps (Customer): Ran both. 54.36.120.11 shows cert chain with missing intermediate and CN mismatch. 3.120.45.9 shows correct chain and SAN includes api.redwood-hosted.com.
Ryan (Oncall): We're going to keep monitoring for TTL-related anomalies. Kara, can you add a scheduled scan that queries common public resolvers and compares IP sets vs our expected pool? If discrepancy > 10% over 5m alert SRE.
Kara (SRE): Yep, adding a probe job and alert rule. Also lowering edge TLS handshake timeout metric baseline to catch regressions earlier.
Maya (Support): Customer happy for now. I've sent mitigation steps and asked them to re-open if they see recurrences. Anything else before we close this thread?
Kara (SRE): I'll leave the probe live and keep this open for 24h. Triage: root cause = stale DNS caching hitting decommissioned host lacking updated cert chain after rotation. Remediation = remove old host, health-check cert validation, customer-side cache flush. Closing once 24h clean.
AcmeOps (Customer): Thanks team, appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
